title: Equality Case of the Weighted Power Mean Chain: WHM = WGM = WAM = WQM ⇔ a = b
description: Answers open question #2 of the weighted power mean chain: the chain WHM ≤ WGM ≤ WAM ≤ WQM collapses to a single value if and only if a = b. We isolate the equality condition for each individual link — WAM = WQM (zero weighted variance), WGM = WAM (AM–GM equality), WHM = WGM (reciprocal duality) — and assemble the headline collapse, plus the strict gap WAM < WQM when a ≠ b and the classical equal-weight specialization HM = GM = AM = QM ⇔ a = b.

meta.author: Formal verification
meta.assumptions: No axioms or sorries. Depends only on the standard foundational axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (verified via #print axioms). Uses Mathlib's weighted AM-GM equality condition.

overview.historicalContext: The classical means HM ≤ GM ≤ AM ≤ QM, and their weighted generalizations, are accompanied by sharp equality conditions: equality holds throughout precisely when all the arguments coincide. This is the two-variable, weighted instance. The unweighted equality case a = b already appears implicitly in Cauchy's original 1821 forward-backward induction proof of AM-GM in the Cours d'Analyse — a different Cauchy result from the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality that names this entry's root file, though both trace to the same convexity toolkit. The equality case of the weighted AM-GM inequality was given a strict-convexity proof by Hardy, Littlewood, and Pólya (*Inequalities*, 1934); Mathlib formalizes it via the strict convexity of the exponential as Real.geom_mean_eq_arith_mean_weighted_iff'.
overview.problemStatement: The parent file proved the weighted power mean chain WHM ≤ WGM ≤ WAM ≤ WQM for positive reals a, b and weights w₁, w₂ > 0 with w₁ + w₂ = 1. Does the equality case WHM = WGM = WAM = WQM ⇔ a = b hold in this weighted setting?
overview.text: We prove that the entire chain collapses to one value iff a = b, isolating the equality condition for each link. The forward direction needs only the WAM = WQM link (zero weighted variance); the backward direction shows every mean collapses to the common value a.
overview.proofStrategy: Three independent equality conditions, then assembly. (1) WAM = WQM ⇔ a = b: square the equality (both sides nonneg), apply the identity w₁a² + w₂b² − (w₁a + w₂b)² = w₁w₂(a−b)²; with w₁,w₂ > 0 this forces (a−b)² = 0. (2) WGM = WAM ⇔ a = b: instantiate Mathlib's AM-GM equality condition at Fin 2 with weights ![w₁,w₂] and values ![a,b]; equality means every value equals the common mean, i.e. a = b. (3) WHM = WGM ⇔ a = b: take reciprocals, which turn WHM into WAM and WGM into WGM of the reciprocals, reducing to (2) at (1/a, 1/b). The headline chain_eq_iff uses link (1) for the forward direction and the collapse-value lemmas for the backward direction.
keyInsights: The weighted-variance identity w₁a² + w₂b² − (w₁a + w₂b)² = w₁w₂(a−b)² is an exact equality (not just ≥ 0), so its vanishing is iff a = b. This makes WAM = WQM the cleanest 'pinch' that drives the whole collapse with nothing beyond ring and Real.sqrt.
Equality cases of inequalities are genuine new content: the parent proved only the ≤ chain, with no information about when equality is attained.
Mathlib's geom_mean_eq_arith_mean_weighted_iff' is the general-Finset AM-GM equality condition; the two-variable case is recovered by packaging weights and values as Fin 2 vectors.
Reciprocal duality WHM(a,b)⁻¹ = WAM(1/a,1/b) and WGM(a,b)⁻¹ = WGM(1/a,1/b) reduces the harmonic–geometric equality to the geometric–arithmetic one for free.
All four means collapse to the common value a when a = b, recovered by simple rpow/sqrt bookkeeping (a^w₁·a^w₂ = a^(w₁+w₂) = a, √((w₁+w₂)a²) = a, etc.).

sections.title: Header: Open Question and Equality-Case Roadmap
sections.summary: Module docstring: states the parent file's open question #2 (does the weighted power-mean equality case extend?), answers YES, lists the individual equality lemmas (WAM=WQM, WGM=WAM, WHM=WGM) plus the headline chain collapse, and sketches the three proof techniques (weighted-variance identity, Mathlib's weighted AM–GM equality condition, reciprocal duality).
sections.mathContext: Chain collapse: $\mathrm{WHM}=\mathrm{WGM}=\mathrm{WAM}=\mathrm{WQM} \iff a=b$, proved via the individual links $\mathrm{WAM}=\mathrm{WQM}\iff a=b$ (weighted-variance identity $w_1a^2+w_2b^2-(w_1a+w_2b)^2=w_1w_2(a-b)^2$), $\mathrm{WGM}=\mathrm{WAM}\iff a=b$ (weighted AM–GM equality), and $\mathrm{WHM}=\mathrm{WGM}\iff a=b$ (reciprocal duality).

sections.title: Weighted Mean Definitions
sections.summary: Four noncomputable defs mirroring the parent: WHM, WGM, WAM, WQM
sections.mathContext: $\text{WHM} = (w_1/a + w_2/b)^{-1}$, $\text{WGM} = a^{w_1} b^{w_2}$, $\text{WAM} = w_1 a + w_2 b$, $\text{WQM} = \sqrt{w_1 a^2 + w_2 b^2}$.

sections.title: Collapse Value at a = b
sections.summary: Each mean equals a when a = b (whm/wgm/wam/wqm_eq_of_eq)
sections.mathContext: At $a = b$: $\text{WHM} = \text{WGM} = \text{WAM} = \text{WQM} = a$, via $a^{w_1+w_2} = a$ and $\sqrt{(w_1+w_2)a^2} = a$.

sections.title: Weighted Variance Identity
sections.summary: Exact identity w₁a² + w₂b² − (w₁a + w₂b)² = w₁w₂(a−b)²
sections.mathContext: The weighted variance equals $w_1 w_2 (a-b)^2$, vanishing iff $a = b$.

sections.title: WAM = WQM ⇔ a = b (Zero Variance)
sections.summary: Squaring + variance identity forces a = b; plus strict WAM < WQM when a ≠ b
sections.mathContext: $w_1 a + w_2 b = \sqrt{w_1 a^2 + w_2 b^2} \iff a = b$, the central pinch.

sections.title: WGM = WAM ⇔ a = b (AM–GM Equality)
sections.mathContext: $a^{w_1} b^{w_2} = w_1 a + w_2 b \iff a = b$, the weighted AM-GM equality case.

sections.title: WHM = WGM ⇔ a = b (Reciprocal Duality)
sections.summary: Reduce to WGM = WAM at (1/a, 1/b) via reciprocals

sections.title: Chain Collapse ⇔ a = b
sections.summary: chain_eq_iff and all_means_eq_iff: the whole chain collapses iff a = b

sections.title: Equal-Weight Specialization
sections.summary: Classical HM = GM = AM = QM ⇔ a = b at w₁ = w₂ = 1/2

conclusion.summary: The weighted power mean chain WHM ≤ WGM ≤ WAM ≤ WQM collapses to a single value if and only if a = b. We give the equality condition for each individual link and assemble the headline collapse, with the WAM = WQM 'zero variance' link as the cleanest driver. The strict gap WAM < WQM for a ≠ b and the classical equal-weight specialization are also recorded.
conclusion.implications: Equality cases sharpen the parent inequality chain into an exact characterization. In probabilistic terms (a, b outcomes with probabilities w₁, w₂), WAM = WQM ⇔ a = b is the statement that the variance vanishes iff the random variable is constant — the equality case of Jensen / Cauchy–Schwarz for a two-point distribution.
openQuestions: Does the n-variable weighted chain admit the same equality characterization WHM = WGM = WAM = WQM ⇔ all aᵢ equal, assembled from Mathlib's general-Finset AM-GM equality condition?
Can the strict monotonicity M_r^w < M_s^w for r < s when the arguments are not all equal be formalized, refining the non-strict power-mean monotonicity?
